overview: Wet, windy systems keep arriving over the Cascades and Coast Mountains through the week, with warmer air and rain at lower elevations. The northern Rockies stay mostly dry until a system arrives Thursday night, with the heavier impacts in western Wyoming Friday into the weekend.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: A low pressure system and its front bring rain and wind to the Cascades through Tuesday night, with snow holding only at higher passes. Another disturbance follows Wednesday night into Thursday. Crystal Mountain leads with 20" in total, with its best day Wednesday at 9". Snow levels rise above pass level by Wednesday evening, so expect more rain than snow.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Snow changes to rain Tuesday as warm air moves in, and rain dominates Wednesday and Thursday. Showers continue into Friday. Whistler's best snow is Tuesday and Wednesday, with 26" in total. Expect mostly rain and wet snow at mid-elevations.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: Light snow ends in western Wyoming Monday evening, and Tuesday through Wednesday stay dry and breezy, with gusts near 30 mph from South Pass through Natrona County. Snow returns Thursday night and Friday. Jackson Hole leads with 9" in total. The NWS is calling for more, 6 to 15 inches Thursday night through Saturday night.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
